http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27933.text: Big News Network.com NATO troops injured in friendly fire training incident Four Italian soldiers were wounded after a machine gunner fired a burst into another armored vehicle in Latvia Four Italian soldiers have been wounded after one of their own troops accidentally opened fire on a fellow armored vehicle during a NATO live-fire exercise in Latvia. The incident occurred late on Friday at the Adazi training area, where Italian forces are deployed as part of NATO's military buildup on the bloc's eastern flank. According to Italy's Defense Ministry, a soldier operating a non-automated weapon mounted on a military vehicle accidentally fired on another Italian vehicle carrying four servicemen. ANSA reported that a burst from a 7.62mm machine gun mounted on a Dardo infantry fighting vehicle raked another Dardo traveling directly ahead, apparently while its rear hatch was open. All four troops, members of Italy's 11th Bersaglieri Regiment, were rushed to a hospital in Riga. One suffered more serious injuries but was reported in stable condition, while none was believed to be in danger of dying. Military investigators are examining how the friendly-fire incident occurred. Around 300 Italian troops are stationed at Camp Adazi as part of NATO's multinational force in Latvia. The military bloc has steadily reinforced its eastern flank and stepped up live-fire drills close to Russia and Belarus, describing the deployments and exercises as "defensive." The growing number of drills has produced a series of serious accidents in the Baltics in recent years. In March 2025, four US soldiers were killed when their 70-ton M88 Hercules recovery vehicle sank into a peat bog at Lithuania's Pabrad training ground, less than 10km from Belarus. At the same range in November, a Belgian soldier died from severe injuries sustained during a live-fire exercise. Days later, several Norwegian troops narrowly escaped being shot when live rounds were fired at targets while soldiers were advancing through woodland behind them. Moscow has repeatedly accused European NATO members of militarizing the continent and preparing for a potential war with Russia. During the BRICS Summit in New Delhi this month, President Vladimir Putin said Western governments were promoting an imaginary 'Russian threat' in order to distract the public from numerous problems in their home countries. https://euobserver.com/239820/lithuania-.text: On Tuesday (22 September), the Lithuanian parliament backed a proposal to lift the constitutional ban on the deployment of nuclear weapons and foreign military bases on the country’s territory. Lithuanian radio LRT reported on the development, which paves the way for nuclear weapons in the country. Lawmakers overwhelmingly approved the constitutional amendment to lift the ban, with 99 votes in favour, 13 against and five abstentions. The proposal must pass two further parliamentary votes, three months apart, before it comes into effect. This comes as Europe as a whole debates nuclear deterrence. In March, French president Emmanuel Macron announced a new French nuclear doctrine. He also raised the possibility of extending France’s nuclear umbrella over countries that could temporarily host French strategic aircraft capable of carrying nuclear weapons. However, the final decision on their use would remain in the hands of the French president. France is the only EU member state with its own nuclear weapons and has a similar number of nuclear warheads to the United Kingdom, which sources them from the US. However, France has long advocated greater autonomy from the US. Macron has justified this due to the inflammatory rhetoric of US president Donald Trump, who puts into question US commitments to European allies. Ten European countries have joined France’s forward deterrence programme: the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Greece, Sweden, Denmark, Norway and Finland, which joined this month ending military neutrality after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. It was in the context of the new European nuclear architecture that MP Remigijus Motuzas, chair of the Lithuanian parliament’s foreign affairs committee, plus another 50 Lithuanian MPs tabled a proposal to lift the constitutional ban on deploying nuclear weapons on the Baltic country’s territory. Lithuania borders Russia’s heavily-militarised Kaliningrad exclave and Belarus, Moscow’s closest ally in its war against Ukraine. “Given the situation we are in, the geopolitical situation and what is happening, I think it is certainly worth it,” parliamentary speaker Juozas Olekas said in May, referring to nuclear deterrence. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters UK weather About 90,000 properties still without power after two storms strike Britain More strong winds are forecast after Storms Boelo and Austen cause travel disruption, flooding and kill two people Tell us: have you been affected by Storm Boelo and Storm Austen Mark Brown North of England correspondent Mon 26 Oct 2026 07.09 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 07.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google About 90,000 properties across northern parts of the UK are still without power after a weekend of stormy weather, with forecasters warning of more strong winds to come. Two men were killed by falling trees after two named storms, Austen and Boelo, pummelled parts of the UK , bringing widespread travel disruption, flooding, power cuts and event cancellations. On Monday morning, the Energy Networks Association, which represents operators in the UK and Ireland, said 90,000 customers were still without power. The association’s chief executive, Lawrence Slade, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that disruption had been widespread with operators having to restore power to about 700,000 customers over the weekend. He said Friday, Saturday and Sunday had been particularly challenging. “It certainly was a tough one. One of the problems was how quickly Boelo followed after Austen.” Storm Boelo causes severe flooding in town centre of Largs, Scotland Another issue was that there was no letup in the strong winds, widely 50-70mph and up to 85mph in northern Scotland . “Until that weather system passes we can’t safely get engineers out to replace poles, to get wires back up etc.” The weather was much milder on Monday but the Met Office said more strong winds were on the way and issued two yellow weather warnings . One is in place from 6pm until 3am on Tuesday, covering western coastal areas from Cornwall up to south-west Scotland. Gusts of up to 65mph could hit exposed coastal areas, accompanied by heavy rain at times. The Met Office warned people to take care near cliffs and be aware of strong waves. The second warning is in place from 3am to 9pm on Tuesday and covers most of Scotland. Forecasters said winds of 50-60mph were likely to be quite widespread with gusts up to 70mph in the far north. It warned of possible travel cancellations, road closures and more power cuts. The weekend storms led to two deaths, authorities said. A 60-year-old man was hit by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway while a man in his 20s died in Finchley, north London. Scotland’s first minister, John Swinney, met senior politicians, emergency teams and forecasters on Sunday to discuss the ongoing response to the weather, amid the warnings of more to come. View image in fullscreen A downed tree in Gladstone Park, London, on Sunday after strong winds overnight. Photograph: Martin Evans/PA On Monday, Swinney posted on X: “My deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the two people who have tragically lost their lives as a result of Storm Boelo. My thoughts are with all those affected by the damage and I thank the emergency services working through the night to keep people safe.” There were also pockets of flooding with dramatic footage from Largs town centre showing flood water cascading through the town centre. One resident said it was the highest she had ever seen in 36 years of living there. Staff at the Thai restaurant Tha-Tien-Thai shared a video of their kitchen overrun by water with the desperate caption: “There is nothing left.” They said its doors would be closed for the foreseeable future “due to larger flood restoration than originally planned”. Emergency services were called to a flooded care home in Saltcoats, North Ayrshire, on Sunday evening. Police Scotland said everyone at the care home was accounted for, road closures were in place and officers were expected to remain on site overnight to assist. There was also travel disruption, with being flights diverted from landing at Leeds Bradford, England’s highest airport, and others cancelled. Most train services were getting back to normal although operators advised customers to check before they travelled. The storms brought a number of event cancellations including the Sunday racing at Aintree, abandoned because of the high winds.
